units.source_text: 即使说我人生最初遇到的难题是美，也并非言过其实。

en.t: It would not be an exaggeration to say that the first difficult problem I encountered in life was beauty.

units.source_text: 父亲是乡间纯朴的僧侣，语汇贫乏，他只告诉我："人世间再没有比金阔更美的东西了。"

en.t: My father was a simple country priest with a poor vocabulary, and he told me only this: "There is nothing in the world more beautiful than Kinkaku."

units.source_text: 我想：在我本知的地方已经存在着美。

en.t: I thought: beauty already existed in a place I had known from the beginning.

units.source_text: 这种思考不由得使我感到不满和焦躁。

en.t: This thought inevitably made me feel dissatisfied and restless.

units.source_text: 因为如果美的确存在那里，那么我的存在就被美疏远了。

en.t: For if beauty truly existed there, then my own existence had been estranged from beauty.
